claim: DN2 to DN4 thymocytes incorporated the most O-propargyl puromycin (OP-Puro) compared to DP and mature single positive thymocytes.
source: Compared to DP and mature single positive thymocytes, DN2 to DN4 thymocytes incorporated the most OP-Puro (Figure 1B), a likely reflection of their high metabolic and proliferative activity (Carpenter and Bosselut, 2010; Kreslavsky et al., 2012; Nagelreiter et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B measuring OP-Puro incorporation across thymocyte subsets, and is also supported by citations to prior literature on metabolic and proliferative activity.

claim: DN4 thymocytes display markedly lower levels of misfolded/unfolded proteins compared to DN2 and DN3 thymocytes despite comparable protein synthesis rates.
source: Intriguingly, despite comparable and high protein synthesis rates across DN2 to DN4 thymocytes, we found that DN4 thymocytes displayed markedly lower levels of misfolded/unfolded proteins (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C measuring misfolded/unfolded proteins using TMI staining.

claim: The DN3-to-DN4 transition is accompanied by induction of proteome quality control mechanisms.
source: These observations suggested that the DN3-to-DN4 transition, which is initiated by β-selection, is accompanied by induction of proteome quality control mechanisms.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that DN4 cells have lower misfolded proteins despite high synthesis rates, suggesting quality control induction.

claim: Expression of ERAD gene Sel1l peaks in DN3 thymocytes.
source: We found elevated expression of the core ERAD (Sel1l) and the UPR (Xbp1, Ddit3 (Chop), Atf4, Dnajb9, and Hspa5 (Bip)) genes in DN3 thymocytes (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative RT-PCR data shown in Figure 1D measuring gene expression across thymocyte subsets.

claim: Expression of UPR genes (Xbp1, Ddit3, Atf4, Dnajb9, and Hspa5) is elevated in DN3 thymocytes.
source: We found elevated expression of the core ERAD (Sel1l) and the UPR (Xbp1, Ddit3 (Chop), Atf4, Dnajb9, and Hspa5 (Bip)) genes in DN3 thymocytes (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative RT-PCR data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Induction of ERAD and UPR genes peaks in the DN3 thymocyte stage in which β-selection is initiated.
source: Notably, induction of these genes peaked in the DN3 thymocyte stage in which β-selection is initiated (Takahama, 2006) and preceded the reduction of misfolded/unfolded proteins in DN4 cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and a citation to prior literature on β-selection timing.

claim: CD2-iCre-mediated deletion of Sel1l results in markedly decreased thymus size and cellularity.
source: Strikingly, CD2-iCre-mediated deletion of the ERAD core component Sel1l (Sel1lflox/flox; CD2-iCre mice, hereafter designated as Sel1l CKO) resulted in a markedly decreased thymus size and cellularity, with significantly reduced and dispersed medullary regions compared to control littermates (Sel1lflox/flox; Ctrl) (Figure 2A–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2A-D measuring thymus size and cellularity.

claim: Sel1l deletion results in a profound reduction of peripheral T cells in the spleen and lymph nodes.
source: The reduced thymus cellularity was accompanied by a profound reduction of peripheral T cells in the spleen and lymph nodes from Sel1l CKO mice compared to control animal (Figure 2—figure supplement 1O–R).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1O–R.

claim: Sel1l deletion has no impact on γδ T cells.
source: Sel1l deletion had no impact on γδ T cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1S), indicating that within the T-cell lineage, SEL1L is selectively required for αβ T cell development.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1S.

claim: SEL1L is selectively required for αβ T cell development within the T-cell lineage.
source: Sel1l deletion had no impact on γδ T cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1S), indicating that within the T-cell lineage, SEL1L is selectively required for αβ T cell development.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Sel1l deletion affects αβ but not γδ T cells.

claim: Deletion of Xbp1 or Perk using hCD2-iCre had no effect on T cell development.
source: Deletion of the UPR mediator Xbp1 or Perk had no effect on T cell development as thymic cellularity, numbers of DN, DP, single positive (SP) thymocytes and splenic T cell numbers were comparable in gene-deficient and littermate control animals (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C–J).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C–J comparing thymocyte populations.

claim: Vav1-iCre-mediated deletion of Atf6a did not perturb thymocyte development.
source: Similarly, Vav1-iCre-mediated deletion of Atf6a which initiates in bone marrow hematopoietic cell progenitors (Joseph et al., 2013) did not perturb thymocyte development (Figure 2—figure supplement 1K–N).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1K–N and a citation about Vav1-iCre activity.

claim: Sel1l-deficiency markedly abrogated DN4 thymocyte generation in OP9-DL1 co-culture.
source: We cultured DN2 thymocytes from control or Sel1l CKO mice on OP9-DL1 cells and found that Sel1l-deficiency markedly abrogated DN4 thymocyte generation (Figure 2K–M).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from OP9-DL1 co-culture shown in Figures 2K-M.

claim: On day 17 of OP9-DL1 co-culture, 71.6% of Sel1l CKO-derived cells remained as DN3 cells compared to 31.3% of control-derived cells.
source: On day 17 of co-culture, only 31.3% DN3 cells remained in control-derived cells, while more than three-fold DN3 cells (71.6%) were found in Sel1l CKO-derived cells (Figure 2K–M), consistent with a block in DN3 to DN4 thymocyte transition.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from OP9-DL1 co-culture shown in Figures 2K-M.

claim: Cell-intrinsic SEL1L activity is required for post β-selection DN thymocyte development.
source: Since only DN3 thymocytes that have successfully undergone β-selection differentiate to the DN4 and DP thymocyte stage, these results reinforce that cell-intrinsic SEL1L activity is required for post β-selection DN thymocyte development.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the OP9-DL1 co-culture data and established knowledge about β-selection.

claim: Sel1l CKO DN4 thymocytes showed more BrdU incorporation than control DN4 thymocytes.
source: Although BrdU incorporation was similar in control and Sel1l CKO DN3 thymocytes, we observed more BrdU incorporation in Sel1l CKO DN4 thymocytes than that in control DN4 thymocytes (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A measuring BrdU incorporation.

claim: Sel1l CKO DN4 thymocytes have less cells in G0 phase and more in G1 and S/G2/M phase compared to control DN4 thymocytes.
source: In agreement, co-staining for Ki-67 and the DNA dye (DAPI) revealed less Sel1l CKO DN4 thymocytes in G0 phase, and more in G1 and S/G2/M phase (Figure 3B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by cell cycle analysis data shown in Figures 3B and 3C.

claim: Sel1l CKO DN3 thymocytes showed higher apoptosis measured by proportions of Annexin-V positive cells in OP9-DL1 co-culture.
source: Indeed, Sel1l CKO DN3 thymocytes showed higher apoptosis measured by proportions of Annexin-V positive cells (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D measuring Annexin-V staining.

claim: Sel1l CKO thymus showed more active Caspase-3 apoptotic cells in the cortex area compared to controls.
source: Compared to controls, Sel1l CKO thymus showed more active Caspase-3 apoptotic cells in the cortex area (Figure 3E,F), which is typically populated by DN thymocytes (Trampont et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figures 3E and 3F, and a citation about cortex composition.

claim: Sel1l-deficient β-selected DN3 cells undergo apoptosis as they differentiate into DN4 thymocytes.
source: Taken together, we concluded that Sel1l-deficient β-selected DN3 cells were undergoing apoptosis as they differentiated into DN4 thymocytes.
evidence: The claim is inferred from multiple apoptosis measurements including Annexin-V, Caspase-3, and TUNEL staining.

claim: Stimulation of EL4 cells with Notch ligand Delta-like 4 (DLL4) induced expression of ERAD genes including Sel1l, Hrd1, Os9, and Edem1.
source: Stimulation of the thymoma cell line EL4 with Notch ligand Delta-like 4 (DLL4) (Camelo et al., 2012; Fitzgerald and Greenwald, 1995) induced expression of the genes involved in ERAD including Sel1l, Hrd1, Os9, and Edem1 as well as SEL1L proteins (Figure 4B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 4B and 4C, and citations about DLL4.

claim: Treatment with DAPT significantly reduced expression of Sel1l, Hrd1, Os9, and Edem1 in DN3 thymocytes.
source: Indeed, treatment with DAPT significantly reduced expression of Notch target genes Hes1, Deltex1, and Ptcra (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B) and also reduced Sel1l, Hrd1, Os9, and Edem1 expression in DN3 thymocytes (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D measuring gene expression after DAPT treatment.

claim: Notch signals regulate expression of genes constituting the ERAD machinery.
source: These data demonstrate that Notch signals regulate expression of genes constituting the ERAD machinery.
evidence: The claim is inferred from DLL4 stimulation and DAPT inhibition experiments showing Notch-dependent ERAD gene expression.

claim: The promoters of Sel1l and Hrd1 contain conserved binding sites for RBP-J.
source: Analysis of the promoters of the core ERAD genes, Sel1l and Hrd1, revealed conserved binding sites for RBP-J (Figure 4E), the DNA binding partner and master transcription factor of the NICD transactivation complex (Castel et al., 2013; Tanigaki and Honjo, 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequence analysis shown in Figure 4E and citations about RBP-J function.

claim: DLL4 stimulation of Notch signaling significantly induced NICD and RBP-J bindings at the promoters of Sel1l, Hrd1, Os9, and Edem.
source: DLL4 stimulation of Notch signaling significantly induced NICD and RBP-J bindings at the promoters of Sel1l, Hrd1, Os9, and Edem (Figure 4F–I).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figures 4F-I.

claim: NICD potently induced both Sel1l and Hrd1 promoter activity in a dose-dependent manner in HEK293T cells.
source: When co-transfected with promoter luciferase reporters into HEK293T cells, NICD potently induced both Sel1l and Hrd1 promoter activity in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 4J).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 4J.

claim: Mutation of the RBP-J-binding sites abolished DLL4-driven induction of Sel1l or Hrd1 luciferase reporter activity.
source: Importantly, mutation of the RBP-J-binding sites abolished DLL4-driven induction of Sel1l or Hrd1 luciferase reporter activity (Figure 4K,L).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data with mutant promoters shown in Figures 4K and 4L.

claim: Notch signaling directly regulates expression of SEL1L ERAD machinery.
source: These data indicate that Notch signaling directly regulates expression of SEL1L ERAD machinery.
evidence: The claim is inferred from ChIP and luciferase reporter data showing direct binding and transcriptional activation.

claim: Sel1l deletion did not affect surface Notch1 protein levels in DN thymocyte populations.
source: Interestingly, although ERAD is known to regulate surface receptor expression in a substrate-specific manner (van den Boomen and Lehner, 2015; Xu et al., 2020), Sel1l deletion did not affect surface Notch1 protein levels in DN thymocyte populations (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C and citations about ERAD substrate specificity.

claim: SEL1L has little impact on the expression of Notch target genes Hes1 and Ptcra in DN3 thymocytes.
source: Similarly, SEL1L had little impact on the expression of Notch target genes Hes1 and Ptcra in DN3 thymocytes (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Thymocyte β-selection defects in Sel1l CKO mice were not due to failure in Notch signal transduction.
source: These results not only suggest that ERAD does not regulate Notch signaling per se but also imply that thymocyte β-selection defects in Sel1l CKO mice were not due to failure in Notch signal transduction.
evidence: The claim is inferred from data showing Sel1l deletion does not affect Notch1 levels or target gene expression.

claim: Sel1l-deficiency does not affect Tcrb gene rearrangement in DN3 and DN4 thymocytes.
source: Genomic DNA analysis of Sel1l-deficient DN3 and DN4 thymocytes showed that recombination of Vb5-Jb2, Vb8-Jb2, and Vb11-Jb2 gene segments were not altered (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), indicating that Sel1l deficiency does not affect Tcrb gene rearrangement.
evidence: The claim is supported by PCR analysis of V(D)J recombination shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Expression of intracellular TCRβ in pre-selected DN3a, post-selected DN3b and DN4 cells was comparable between control and Sel1l CKO mice.
source: Expression of intracellular TCRβ in pre-selected DN3a, post-selected DN3b and DN4 cells was comparable between control and Sel1l CKO mice (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: Sel1l deletion had no impact on the expression of pre-TCR signaling intermediates including LCK and ZAP-70 in DN3 and DN4 thymocytes.
source: Sel1l deletion also had no impact on the expression of pre-TCR signaling intermediates including LCK and ZAP-70 in DN3 and DN4 thymocytes (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The OT-II TCR transgene did not rescue T cell development in OT-II. Sel1l CKO mice.
source: However, the OT-II TCR transgene did not rescue T cell development in OT-II. Sel1l CKO mice which showed a >80% decrease in thymic cellularity, DP and SP thymocytes (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1E–G comparing OT-II transgenic mice.

claim: β-selection defects in Sel1l CKO mice were not due to defects in pre-TCR expression or signaling.
source: Taken together, these data implied that β-selection defects in Sel1l CKO mice were not due to defects in pre-TCR expression or signaling.
evidence: The claim is inferred from data showing normal TCRβ expression, signaling intermediates, and lack of rescue by TCR transgene.

claim: The most upregulated pathways in Sel1l CKO DN3 thymocytes were ER stress response and the UPR, including both IRE1α and PERK pathways.
source: The most upregulated pathways in Sel1l CKO DN3 thymocytes were ER stress response and the UPR, including both IRE1α and PERK pathways (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data and pathway analysis shown in Figures 5A and 5B.

claim: Sel1l CKO DN3 cells showed significant ER expansion compared to control thymocytes.
source: Consistent with elevated ER stress, flow cytometry quantification of ER tracker dye staining indicated significant ER expansion in Sel1l CKO DN3 cells compared to control thymocytes (Figure 5F,G).
evidence: The claim is supported by ER tracker staining data shown in Figures 5F and 5G.

claim: Sel1l CKO thymocytes showed a significant increase in IRE1α proteins and in the splicing of its substrate Xbp1.
source: We found a significant increase in IRE1α proteins and in the splicing of its substrate Xbp1 in Sel1l CKO thymocytes (Figure 5H,I and Figure 5—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot and PCR data shown in Figures 5H, 5I and Figure 5—figure supplement 2A,B.

claim: Sel1l CKO DN3 thymocytes showed increased PERK and eIF2α phosphorylation as well as increased ATF4 and BIP proteins.
source: We also observed increased PERK and eIF2α phosphorylation as well as increased ATF4 and BIP proteins in Sel1l CKO DN3 thymocytes (Figure 5H).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5H.

claim: Various ER chaperones and other members of ERAD pathway were markedly upregulated in Sel1l CKO DN3 and DN4 thymocytes.
source: Various ER chaperones, including Calreticulin, Grp94 (Hsp90b1), Hspa5(Bip), Hyou1, and Canx, and other members of ERAD pathway were markedly upregulated in Sel1l CKO DN3 and DN4 thymocytes (Figure 5—figure supplement 2C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2C,D.

claim: Sel1l deletion triggers ER stress leading to activation of all three UPR branches in DN thymocytes.
source: These data indicate that Sel1l deletion triggers ER stress leading to activation of all three UPR branches in DN thymocytes.
evidence: The claim is inferred from data showing activation of IRE1α, PERK, and ATF6 pathways.

claim: Sel1l CKO DN3 thymocytes exhibited significantly higher staining for misfolded/unfolded proteins with TMI.
source: Indeed, we found that Sel1l CKO DN3 thymocytes exhibited significantly higher staining for misfolded/unfolded proteins with TMI (Figure 5J,K).
evidence: The claim is supported by TMI staining data shown in Figures 5J and 5K.

claim: Sel1l CKO DN3 thymocytes displayed more protein aggregates compared with control thymocytes.
source: Sel1l CKO DN3 thymocytes displayed more protein aggregates compared with control thymocytes (Figure 5M,N).
evidence: The claim is supported by ProteoStat staining data shown in Figures 5M and 5N.

claim: DN thymocytes lacking SEL1L accumulate misfolded/unfolded proteins leading to proteotoxic stress that triggers the UPR and eventually apoptosis.
source: Collectively, these results corroborate that DN thymocytes lacking SEL1L accumulate misfolded/unfolded proteins leading to proteotoxic stress that then trigged the UPR and eventually apoptosis.
evidence: The claim is inferred from multiple measurements of misfolded proteins, UPR activation, and apoptosis.

claim: Sel1l/Xbp1 double-knockout mice showed more severe thymocyte development defects including a more than 95% loss in thymus cellularity and DP thymocyte numbers.
source: In fact, Sel1l/Xbp1 double-knockout (DKO) mice showed more severe thymocytes development defects including a more than 95% loss in thymus cellularity and DP thymocyte numbers (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Induction of the IRE1α/XBP1 pathway functions as a compensatory adaptative pathway to restrain Sel1l-deficiency induced ER stress.
source: These data suggest that induction of the IRE1α/XBP1 pathway functions as a compensatory adaptative pathway to restrain Sel1l-deficiency induced ER stress.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Xbp1 deletion worsens the Sel1l CKO phenotype.

claim: Deletion of Perk significantly rescued the Sel1l CKO mouse phenotype evident in the near complete restoration of thymus cellularity, DP and SP thymocyte cell numbers.
source: In contrast to deletion of Xbp1, we found that deletion of Perk significantly rescued the Sel1l CKO mouse phenotype evident in the near complete restoration of thymus cellularity, DP and SP thymocyte cell numbers (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 6A and 6B comparing double knockout mice.

claim: Perk deletion restored peripheral T cells in spleen and lymph nodes compared to Sel1l CKO mice.
source: Perk deletion also restored peripheral T cells in spleen and lymph nodes compared to Sel1l CKO mice (Figure 6C–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 6C-F.

claim: Perk deletion significantly reduced Sel1l-deficiency induced Chop induction.
source: Consistent with the rescue, Perk deletion significantly reduced Sel1l-deficiency induced Chop induction (Figure 6G) and thymocyte apoptosis (Figure 6H,I) and restored normal cell cycle kinetics to Sel1l CKO DN4 thymocytes (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 6G.

claim: Perk deletion reduced thymocyte apoptosis in Sel1l CKO mice.
source: Consistent with the rescue, Perk deletion significantly reduced Sel1l-deficiency induced Chop induction (Figure 6G) and thymocyte apoptosis (Figure 6H,I) and restored normal cell cycle kinetics to Sel1l CKO DN4 thymocytes (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figures 6H and 6I.

claim: Activated PERK signaling contributed to the apoptosis of DN3/DN4 thymocytes that impaired β-selection in Sel1l CKO mice.
source: As Perk deficiency alone had no effect on T cell development (Figure 6A–I), these results indicate that activated PERK signaling contributed to the apoptosis of DN3/DN4 thymocytes that impaired β-selection in Sel1l CKO mice.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the rescue of Sel1l CKO phenotype by Perk deletion and the lack of phenotype in Perk single knockout.

claim: SEL1L-ERAD promotes β-selected DN thymocyte differentiation by maintaining ER proteostasis and suppressing ER stress-induced cell death through the PERK pathway.
source: Collectively, we conclude that SEL1L-ERAD promotes β-selected DN thymocyte differentiation by maintaining ER proteostasis and suppressing ER stress-induced cell death through the PERK pathway.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the collective data showing Sel1l maintains proteostasis, prevents ER stress, and that PERK drives apoptosis in its absence.

claim: ERAD is the master regulator of physiological ER proteostasis in immature DN thymocytes.
source: Here, we show that ERAD is the master regulator of physiological ER proteostasis in immature DN thymocytes.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the severe phenotype of ERAD deficiency and lack of phenotype from individual UPR component deletions.

claim: The ERAD machinery was critically required for successful β-selection of DN3 thymocytes.
source: The ERAD machinery was critically required for successful β-selection of DN3 thymocytes and consequently, ERAD deficiency impeded αβ T cell development.
evidence: The claim is supported by data showing DN3 to DN4 transition defects and subsequent developmental blocks.

claim: ERAD selectively preserves the cellular fitness of αβ, but not γδ T lymphocytes.
source: Intriguingly, ERAD selectively preserves the cellular fitness of αβ, but not γδ T lymphocytes.
evidence: The claim is supported by data showing normal γδ T cell numbers in Sel1l CKO mice.

claim: Notch signaling directly regulates ERAD gene expression to promote the integrity of ER proteostasis during β-selection.
source: We found that Notch signaling directly regulates ERAD gene expression to promote the integrity of ER proteostasis during β-selection.
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP data showing direct binding and luciferase data showing transcriptional activation.

claim: Activation of ERAD restricts PERK-dependent cell death in DN3 thymocytes during β-selection.
source: Activation of ERAD restricts PERK-dependent cell death in DN3 thymocytes during β-selection.
evidence: The claim is inferred from data showing PERK-driven apoptosis in ERAD-deficient cells and rescue by PERK deletion.

claim: Genetic inactivation of Perk rescued β-selection in Sel1l-deficient thymocytes.
source: Genetic inactivation of Perk rescued β-selection in Sel1l-deficient thymocytes.
evidence: The claim is supported by data showing restoration of thymocyte development in Sel1l/Perk double knockout mice.

claim: Individual UPR regulators are dispensable for β-selection and subsequent stages of thymocyte maturation.
source: Unlike the marked defect in thymocyte development in the absence of SEL1L-ERAD, our current study now clearly demonstrates that individual UPR regulators are dispensable for β-selection and subsequent stages of thymocyte maturation.
evidence: The claim is supported by data showing normal T cell development in Xbp1, Perk, and Atf6 single knockout mice.

claim: Induction of the SEL1L axis of ERAD, which peaks at the DN3 stage, represents a previously undefined and critical ER proteostasis checkpoint during β-selection.
source: Thus, induction of the SEL1L axis of ERAD, which peaks at the DN3 stage, represents a previously undefined and critical ER proteostasis checkpoint during β-selection.
evidence: The claim is inferred from data showing peak ERAD expression in DN3 cells and requirement for β-selection.

claim: This ER proteostasis checkpoint is regulated by the same Notch signals which, together with the pre-TCR, induce β-selection in DN3 thymocytes.
source: It is notable that this ER proteostasis checkpoint is also regulated by the same Notch signals which, together with the pre-TCR, induce β-selection in DN3 thymocytes.
evidence: The claim is inferred from data showing Notch directly regulates ERAD genes and established knowledge about Notch's role in β-selection.

claim: Notch1 and RBP-J directly bind to most ERAD gene promoters and directly regulate their expression.
source: We identified that Notch1 and RBP-J directly bind to most ERAD gene promoters and directly regulate their expression.
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data showing binding to ERAD gene promoters.

claim: Notch-signal induced SEL1L protein levels exceeded the change in Sel1l mRNA expression, suggesting additional post-transcriptional regulation of ERAD by Notch.
source: In fact, we observed that Notch-signal induced SEL1L protein levels exceeded the change in Sel1l mRNA expression (Figure 4B,C), suggesting additional post-transcriptional regulation of ERAD by Notch that warrants further investigation.
evidence: The claim is inferred from comparing mRNA and protein level changes shown in Figures 4B and 4C.

claim: ERAD is responsible for the clearance of misfolded proteins at steady-state and is constitutively activated regardless of ER stress.
source: ERAD is responsible for the clearance of misfolded proteins at steady-state and is constitutively activated regardless of ER stress.
evidence: The claim draws from established scientific knowledge about ERAD function.

claim: The UPR is a stress response pathway that is triggered when the accumulation of misfolded and unfolded proteins exceed the ER folding capacity.
source: In contrast, the UPR is a stress response pathway that is triggered when the accumulation of misfolded and unfolded proteins exceed the ER folding capacity.
evidence: The claim draws from established scientific knowledge about UPR function.

claim: The IRE1α-XBP1 axis is essential for eosinophil, dendritic cell, NK, and plasma cell differentiation.
source: For instance, the IRE1α-XBP1 is essential for eosinophil (Bettigole et al., 2015), dendritic cell (Cubillos-Ruiz et al., 2015; Iwakoshi et al., 2007; Osorio et al., 2014), NK (Dong et al., 2019; Wang et al., 2019), and plasma cell (Reimold et al., 2001; Shapiro-Shelef and Calame, 2005) differentiation.
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Sel1l-deficiency impaired the survival of DN thymocytes following β selection and resulted in the inability of DN3 thymocytes to expand and progress to DP thymocytes.
source: Sel1l-deficiency impaired the survival of DN thymocytes following β selection and resulted in the inability of DN3 thymocytes to expand and progress to DP thymocytes.
evidence: The claim is supported by data showing increased apoptosis and developmental block.

claim: This phenotype was not due to defective rearrangement of TCRβ nor defective Notch or pre-TCR signaling.
source: Interestingly, this phenotype was not due to defective rearrangement of TCRβ nor defective Notch or pre-TCR signaling which both activate pro-survival genes in β-selected thymocytes (Ciofani and Zúñiga-Pflücker, 2005; Kreslavsky et al., 2012; Zhao et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by data showing normal TCRβ rearrangement, Notch signaling, and pre-TCR signaling, along with citations.

claim: Only PERK axis induces apoptosis in Sel1l CKO thymocytes among the three UPR pathways.
source: While all three UPR pathways can promote apoptosis and appear to be upregulated in Sel1l CKO thymocytes, it is notable that only PERK axis induces apoptosis in Sel1l CKO thymocytes.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the selective rescue by PERK deletion and worsening by XBP1 deletion.

claim: Induction of the IRE1α-XBP1 axis of the UPR can help cells adapt to stress.
source: On the contrary, induction of the IRE1α-XBP1 axis of the UPR can help cells adapt to stress.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the worsening of phenotype when XBP1 is deleted in Sel1l CKO mice.

claim: Deletion of Xbp1 in Sel1l CKO thymocytes exacerbated defects in thymocyte development unlike PERK inactivation which restored T cell development from Sel1l CKO thymocytes.
source: Consistent with this view, deletion of Xbp1 in Sel1l CKO thymocytes exacerbated defects in thymocyte development unlike PERK inactivation which restored T cell development from Sel1l CKO thymocytes.
evidence: The claim is supported by data comparing double knockout phenotypes.

claim: DN thymocytes undergoing β selection expand more than 100-fold.
source: In addition, DN thymocytes undergoing β selection expand more than 100-fold, a situation that likely explains their increased translational activity.
evidence: The claim draws from established knowledge about β-selection and is consistent with observed translational activity.

claim: Upregulation of the SEL1L-ERAD axis in DN3 thymocytes provides a mechanism to alleviate deleterious proteotoxic stress that compromise the fitness of DN4 thymocytes.
source: That post-β-selected DN thymocytes displayed markedly low levels of misfolded/unfolded proteins support the view that upregulation of the SEL1L-ERAD axis in DN3 thymocytes provides a mechanism to alleviate deleterious proteotoxic stress that compromise the fitness of DN4 thymocytes.
evidence: The claim is inferred from data showing low misfolded proteins in DN4 cells and high ERAD expression in DN3 cells.

claim: SEL1L-ERAD safeguards the DN3/DN4 thymocyte pool to ensure that the maximum number of DN thymocytes expressing a functional TCRβ protein progress to the DP stage to audition for positive selection.
source: In this way, SEL1L-ERAD safeguards to DN3/DN4 thymocyte pool to ensure that the maximum number of DN thymocytes expressing a functional TCRβ protein progress to the DP stage to audition for positive selection.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the role of ERAD in maintaining thymocyte fitness during β-selection.

claim: Activating NOTCH1 mutations are found in more than 50% of human T cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL) patients.
source: Activating NOTCH1 mutations are found in more than 50% of human T cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL) patients (Weng et al., 2004) wherein Notch plays pivotal roles in regulating the survival and metabolism of T-ALL cells (Aster et al., 2011; García-Peydró et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature on T-ALL.

claim: Notch plays pivotal roles in regulating the survival and metabolism of T-ALL cells.
source: Activating NOTCH1 mutations are found in more than 50% of human T cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL) patients (Weng et al., 2004) wherein Notch plays pivotal roles in regulating the survival and metabolism of T-ALL cells (Aster et al., 2011; García-Peydró et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: In addition to driving energy metabolism and survival programs demanded by proliferating thymocytes following β-selection, Notch signals in parallel activate the ERAD machinery in DN3 thymocytes to clear misfolded proteins.
source: We propose that in addition to driving energy metabolism and survival programs demanded by proliferating thymocytes following β-selection, Notch signals in parallel activate the ERAD machinery in DN3 thymocytes to clear misfolded proteins.
evidence: The claim is a proposed model based on the data showing Notch regulates ERAD and ERAD is required for β-selection.

claim: Stringent protein quality control through the SEL1L-ERAD pathway is required for successful β-selection and the development of the αβ T cells that mediate adaptive immunity.
